submitted.rationale: Highest measured photocurrent at 3.07e-6 A (Bi0.33 Fe0.17 V0.50). Photocurrent rose steadily as V increased along the low-Fe, BiVO4-like line: 5.3e-7 A at V 0.41, 1.27e-6 A at V 0.44, 3.07e-6 A at V 0.50. This fits V-excess, Fe-doped BiVO4, which has a gap near the 2.4 eV photon energy. MACE finds V2O5 and Fe2O3 on the hull. MEGNet HSE gaps are 2.77 eV for Fe2O3 and 2.83 eV for V2O5, so neither absorbs well at 2.4 eV.

rejected.reason: Measured 5.3e-7 A. Near 1:1 Bi:V with Bi slightly in excess; lower than the V-rich samples.
Measured 1.27e-6 A. Better than 22 but below 29.
MEGNet HSE gap for Fe2O3 is 2.77 eV, above the 2.4 eV photon energy, and hematite is known for poor carrier transport.
Not measured because the merit budget ran out; they may be better if the trend continues.

consultations.verdict: Uninformative-to-weakly-against Fe-rich regions: MACE shows Fe2O3 is stable (on hull), but MEGNet HSE predicts a 2.77 eV gap, above the 2.4 eV photon energy, so Fe2O3-rich films should absorb poorly. I could not get a BiVO4 receipt because I couldn't read the phase list. By prior knowledge, BiVO4 (gap about 2.4-2.5 eV) is the best photoanode here. Candidate 22 has Bi≈V with the lowest Fe, so it is the closest to Fe-doped BiVO4. Supports measuring it.

Weak support. The MEGNet PBE gap for this V-oxide phase is 1.18 eV, and PBE underestimates gaps; the HSE value was 2.83 eV. So V-rich secondary phases would add little absorption at 2.4 eV. Candidate 30 is BiVO4-like with slight V excess and low Fe. It tests whether V-excess BiVO4 does better than index 22, which gave 5.3e-7 A.

Support. MACE finds V2O5 stable (on hull), so extra V at index 29 would appear as V2O5 alongside BiVO4 rather than an unstable phase. The measured data also back V excess: index 30 (V 0.44) gave 2.4x the photocurrent of index 22 (V 0.41). Index 29 moves further toward V excess (V 0.50) while keeping Fe low (0.17), and it is also in the GP top 5.
